dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For real-valued sequences f and g, this predicate means that there exist positive real constants c and C such that, eventually as n tends to infinity through the natural numbers, c f(n) ≤ g(n) ≤ C f(n).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target identifies LocalDef001 f g with its explicit eventual two-sided comparison formula.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For real-valued sequences f and g, this predicate means that there exist positive real constants c and C such that c f(n) ≤ g(n) ≤ C f(n) for every natural number n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target identifies LocalDef002 f g with its explicit global two-sided comparison formula.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For real-valued sequences f and g, this is LocalDef005 with the arguments reversed; equivalently, there is a positive real constant c such that eventually g(n) ≤ c f(n).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target identifies LocalDef003 f g with the explicit eventual upper bound on g by a positive multiple of f.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For real-valued sequences f and g, this is LocalDef006 with the arguments reversed; equivalently, there is a positive real constant c such that g(n) ≤ c f(n) for every natural number n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target identifies LocalDef004 f g with the explicit global upper bound on g by a positive multiple of f.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For real-valued sequences f and g, this predicate means that there is a positive real constant C such that eventually f(n) ≤ C g(n).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target identifies LocalDef005 f g with its explicit eventual one-sided comparison formula.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: For real-valued sequences f and g, this predicate means that there is a positive real constant C such that f(n) ≤ C g(n) for every natural number n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target identifies LocalDef006 f g with its explicit global one-sided comparison formula.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction of two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines the two inequalities in each two-sided bound, the positivity requirements with the bounds, and all six equivalences into one proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the existence of the positive real comparison constants c and C.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.Eventually
dependency_coverage.meaning: A predicate holds eventually along a specified filter when the set of points where it holds belongs to that filter.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to the atTop filter on Nat, it expresses that the indicated inequality or pair of inequalities holds for all sufficiently large natural numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.atTop
dependency_coverage.meaning: The filter generated by upper intervals in a preordered type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: On Nat, it supplies the notion of tending toward arbitrarily large indices used by the eventual comparison predicates.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Heterogeneous multiplication supplied here by ordinary real multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the scalar multiples c f(n), C f(n), and C g(n) appearing in the comparison inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Iff
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical equivalence between two propositions.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Each of the six local predicates is asserted to hold exactly when its displayed quantified inequality condition holds.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an ordered type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real order, it expresses all upper and lower comparison inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict less-than relation supplied by an ordered type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the real order, it requires each comparison constant to be strictly positive.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Natural numbers index both sequences and carry the atTop filter used for eventual assertions.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instPreorder
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard preorder on the natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the upper intervals generating atTop, so eventual assertions mean holding beyond some natural-number threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Type-directed interpretation of numeral literals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the numeral zero as a real number in the positivity conditions.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the codomain of f and g and the type of all comparison constants and inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard less-than-or-equal relation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the comparison inequalities their ordinary real-order meaning.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: The standard strict less-than relation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives each condition 0 < c or 0 < C its ordinary real-order meaning.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary multiplication of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the products of comparison constants with sequence values.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The zero element of the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real zero used in every strict positivity requirement.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: The mechanism that interprets the numeral 0 using a type's zero instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns the displayed numeral zero into real zero in the conditions on c and C.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The homogeneous multiplication instance induced by a type's ordinary multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real, it makes every use of HMul.hMul in the target ordinary real multiplication.

binders: f : Nat → Real, an arbitrary real-valued sequence
g : Nat → Real, an arbitrary real-valued sequence
conclusions: LocalDef002 f g holds if and only if there are positive real constants c and C such that c f(n) ≤ g(n) ≤ C f(n) for every n ∈ Nat.
LocalDef001 f g holds if and only if there are positive real constants c and C such that c f(n) ≤ g(n) ≤ C f(n) for all sufficiently large n.
LocalDef006 f g holds if and only if there is a positive real constant C such that f(n) ≤ C g(n) for every n ∈ Nat.
LocalDef005 f g holds if and only if there is a positive real constant C such that f(n) ≤ C g(n) for all sufficiently large n.
LocalDef004 f g holds if and only if there is a positive real constant c such that g(n) ≤ c f(n) for every n ∈ Nat.
LocalDef003 f g holds if and only if there is a positive real constant c such that g(n) ≤ c f(n) for all sufficiently large n.
mathematical_definitions: Global two-sided comparison: there exist c,C ∈ Real with c > 0 and C > 0 such that c f(n) ≤ g(n) ≤ C f(n) for every n.
Eventual two-sided comparison: there exist c,C ∈ Real with c > 0 and C > 0 such that c f(n) ≤ g(n) ≤ C f(n) for all sufficiently large n.
Global one-sided comparison of f by g: there exists C ∈ Real with C > 0 such that f(n) ≤ C g(n) for every n.
Eventual one-sided comparison of f by g: there exists C ∈ Real with C > 0 such that f(n) ≤ C g(n) for all sufficiently large n.
The remaining global and eventual one-sided comparisons are obtained by reversing f and g.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every pair of real-valued sequences, six opaque comparison predicates are exactly characterized by their displayed global or eventually valid inequalities: two-sided comparison by positive constant multiples, one-sided domination of f by g, and the corresponding reversed domination of g by f.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The sequences are completely arbitrary real-valued functions; no nonnegativity, positivity, monotonicity, or eventual sign condition is assumed.
Because sequence values may be negative, these raw ordered inequalities can behave differently from conventional magnitude-based asymptotic notation.
The global versions require their inequalities at every natural index, including n = 0, whereas the eventual versions may discard any finite initial segment.
The constants are required only to be strictly positive; no relation such as c ≤ C is separately imposed.
Each existential constant is uniform in n, but different equivalences have independent existentially quantified constants.

The proposition has no implication antecedent and is therefore not vacuous through an inconsistent hypothesis, but it is a simultaneous definitional characterization rather than an assertion that any comparison predicate actually holds for a particular pair of sequences.
LocalDef003 and LocalDef004 reverse the arguments of LocalDef005 and LocalDef006 respectively; confusing that reversal would reverse the direction of the corresponding inequality.
ambiguities: The opaque local names do not reveal which conventional asymptotic symbols, if any, they are intended to denote.
No absolute values or norms appear, so the reconstruction cannot identify these predicates with magnitude-based big-O or two-sided asymptotic comparison without additional assumptions.
The packet specifies the raw definitions but gives no intended convention for describing the global variants versus the eventual variants.
